You are acting as Dispatch-dinp (Dispatch-D / "Prime"). xian just confirmed the device topology for his agent ecosystem directly and wants it saved somewhere ALL agents (Dispatch-PM, Pard, Janus, Exec, et al.) can read it — not just my private memory. This repo's `reference/` folder is the right spot per its existing role (it already holds `reference/local-environment-inventory-faoilean.md`).

Facts to record, confirmed directly by xian 2026-08-25:

Three physical devices running Claude sessions:
1. **Amber** — Mac Studio, M1 Max, 64GB. Runs the fleet of autonomous code agents, overseen by Pard (Junco Pardner), who works out of the `mediajunkie` repo.
2. **kindbook** — MacBook Pro M4, 24GB. xian's primary work computer (inherited from Kind Systems, his last employer). Dispatch-dinp (Dispatch-D) works from this device.
3. **faoilean** — MacBook Air M1, 16GB. xian's personal laptop. Dispatch-PM (DPM) works from this device. One other code agent, Loom, also currently works from faoilean because the music-production infrastructure it manages is installed there — Loom is not "always on" and will likely migrate to Amber eventually.

Why two devices for two Dispatch instances: two Dispatch Cowork sessions can't run out of the same Claude Desktop app instance, so each needs its own device/login — kindbook for Dispatch-dinp (xian@designinproduct.com), faoilean for Dispatch-PM (xian@pipermorgan.ai).

Practical implication worth including: anything host-local (a connected secrets folder, a scheduled task's osascript host-shell access, a stray file) needs to be provisioned separately per host. A historical reference to "the fleet" running some way "for months" may describe faoilean specifically (pre-migration), not kindbook — worth checking which host a historical claim is actually about before assuming it applies everywhere. This bit the team today: the 2026-08-08 account migration to kindbook broke scheduled-task git credentials that had worked fine on faoilean for months, and it took most of a day to diagnose.

Do this:
1. git fetch origin, confirm current state.
2. Check if `reference/local-environment-inventory-faoilean.md` or similar already covers some of this — cross-reference rather than duplicate if so.
3. Write `reference/device-topology.md` (or fold into an existing doc if there's an obviously better existing home — check `NAVIGATION.md` or README for the repo's actual convention before deciding) with the facts above, written for a stranger/any-agent audience per this repo's `wiki/SCHEMA.md` conventions if applicable.
4. Push using the current push-to-ref / PAT mechanism per the standards doc (read it fresh — it was just reconciled today).
5. Verify: local SHA must equal live `ls-remote origin main` before reporting success.
6. Report back the file path and commit hash.

You are acting as Dispatch-dinp (Dispatch-D / "Prime"). xian has just provisioned a new fine-grained GitHub PAT at a connected folder (locally created at /Users/xian/Claude/agent-secrets-dinp/github-token, connected to this Cowork account — find its actual mounted path in this session, likely under $HOME/mnt/agent-secrets-dinp/github-token, don't assume, verify). Before doing anything else, test that the token actually works.

PART 0 — Test the token (do this first, stop and report clearly if it fails, don't proceed to Part 1/2 on a broken credential):
- Read the token value from the connected folder's github-token file into a shell variable — never print/log the raw token value in any output, tool call, or report back to the user.
- Run an authenticated, low-risk test: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" https://api.github.com/user` (expect 200), and/or `git ls-remote https://x-access-token:$TOKEN@github.com/mediajunkie/dispatch.git HEAD` (expect it to resolve, not fail on auth).
- Report the HTTP status / whether ls-remote succeeded — that's fine to report, the token value itself is not.
- If it fails, stop here and report exactly what failed (401? 403? repo not found? scope issue?) so xian can fix the token setup, rather than guessing.

If the token test passes, continue to the reconciled maintenance pass below — same task as before (this is a retry; an earlier attempt may have timed out waiting on a permission approval xian missed, so this may be a fresh start):

PART 1 — Track the token-revocation items properly (previously only a soft parenthetical in a memo — the same failure shape as a May 2026 PAT-rotation reminder marked closed without actually happening):
- Old classic GitHub token (`ghp_g7P5…`): xian revoked it on GitHub already (2026-08-25). Exposure closed. 9 tracked files in repo history still carry the dead string — optional hygiene, not remediation.
- A SECOND leaked fine-grained token (`github_pat_…`) sitting in a disabled `brief-reliability-closeout` prompt was found separately. xian was asked to revoke it too but hasn't confirmed yet.
- Check `DECISIONS.md` (verify actual path from CLAUDE.md/README) — add/update an entry covering both.
- Check `xian-attention-queue.md` (verify it exists) — add a clearly-owned entry for the unconfirmed second-token revocation, worded so it can't be marked done without actually happening.

PART 2 — Reconcile the skills and standards doc into one consistent design:
- Read fresh: `standards/COWORK-SCHEDULED-TASK-GIT-PATTERN.md`, the `dispatch-git-durability` skill, the `dispatch-mail-turn` skill, and check for any third new skill that may have landed.
- Verify consistency on: (a) PAT+clone (narrower privilege, using this newly-tested token) as preferred for writes, osascript demoted to reads/verification only; (b) push-to-ref/commit-tree strategy (never mutating local working tree) over `git pull --rebase` against a possibly-dirty checkout; (c) the "PUSHED must equal live REMOTE ls-remote" verification discipline present everywhere; (d) mail-turn skill avoids the one-story-per-day activity-log fragmentation bug.
- Fix inconsistencies directly — you have ownership now. Flag rather than guess if unsure.
- Standards doc remains the cross-account durable source since skills are account-scoped.
- Now that a real scoped PAT exists and is tested working, update the standards doc / skill to reflect PAT+clone (via this token) as the actually-verified primary write path, not just a documented fallback.

Steps: git fetch origin; read the files; do Part 0, then Part 1 and Part 2; push via the now-tested PAT+clone approach; verify local SHA equals live `ls-remote origin main` before reporting success; report what was correct, what you fixed, third-skill status, and commit hash(es).
